# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
M1. A DELETE THAT DID NOT DELETE, AND A CHECK THAT AGREED WITH IT. The
    throwaway urllib probe was removed with `rm -f tools/bm_probe_unlisted.py`
    from a shell whose working directory was already tools/, so it targeted
    tools/tools/... and -f swallowed the miss. The `ls` I ran to confirm ran
    from the same wrong directory and reported the file absent, so my own
    verification agreed with my own mistake. The CONTROL caught it on the
    next run, naming the file. Verify with the control, never with a second
    reading that shares the first one's assumption.

M2. A PORT CAN BE CORRECT AND STILL WRONG. See the buffering note in 01: the
    Python session-start printed exactly the right lines in the wrong order
    because a pipe is buffered and a shell's children are not. Diffing both
    streams on a fixture that actually produces output is what caught it; a
    test asserting "the digest appears" would have passed.

M3. THE BATTERY FOUND WHAT THE PER-SUITE RUNS COULD NOT. After the port I ran
    every suite that obviously touches hooks and they were green. The full
    battery then found tools/test_bm_view.py asserting the Stop contract by
    counting strings in the hook command, which the port had emptied. It was
    a false alarm rather than a break, and it was in the one suite nobody
    would search for hook wiring. Run the whole thing, not the parts you can
    predict.

M4. MY OWN NEW TOOL SHIPPED A BUG THE TEST LATER PINNED. The first draft of
    scripts/bm_ci_context.py read `git cat-file -e` printing NOTHING as
    failure, so every present commit looked absent and a healthy pull request
    pipeline would have been refused. Caught by running it against a commit
    the clone demonstrably had. The suite now pins that exact case.

M5. A REFUSAL I DID NOT WRITE DOWN AS A PASS. tools/test_bm_packaging_install.py
    skips its only test without a pip index and therefore runs zero tests,
    which the gate counts as a failure by its own rule. That is the rule
    working, and it is in the baseline as well as in the branch run, so it is
    an environment fact rather than a regression. Recorded because a reader
    comparing the two summaries will see a red suite in both and should know
    why.
<!-- bm-human:end -->
